description:
Karnity Castle stands beside Lake Kocioł near Miłomłyn, in Warmia-Masuria, a large red-brick building in the Romantic neo-Gothic style. An octagonal corner tower and a rectangular tower facing the lake give the castle its distinctive silhouette. It was built in the mid-1850s — sources give either 1855 or 1856 — and one hotel listing credits the von Albedyhll family as its builders, though this attribution is not independently confirmed beyond that source.

The castle's lakeside setting is as much a part of the experience as the building itself: a private beach area sits on Lake Kocioł, with water-sports equipment available to rent, and guests can relax on a terrace or make use of a sauna after a day outdoors.

Today Karnity operates as a hotel, with the former riding school on the grounds converted into additional guest accommodation. It is worth noting that this is a 19th-century Romantic-era castle rather than a medieval fortress.

faqs.question: Is Karnity a medieval castle?
faqs.answer: No. The present red-brick neo-Gothic building dates from the mid-1850s (sources give 1855 or 1856).

faqs.answer: On the rate we saw (around €80 for a Double or Twin Room), yes.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** At Karnity 10, near Miłomłyn in Warmia-Masuria, beside Lake Kocioł.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €80/night for a 15 m² Double or Twin Room with a private bathroom and flat-screen TV, with breakfast included, free cancellation and no prepayment on the rate seen; about €1 in taxes is shown separately. Lake-view apartments of 30 m² with a spa tub start around €160.

**On-site:** A private beach area on the lake, water-sports equipment rental, a sauna and a sunny terrace.

**Good to know:** This is a 19th-century neo-Gothic castle rather than a medieval one, and the lake setting is the main draw. Accommodation is spread across the castle complex and converted buildings such as the former riding school, so ask which building your room is in.

**Combine with:** [Olsztyn Castle](/castles/poland/olsztyn-castle-warmia) and [Ryn Castle](/castles/poland/ryn-castle), elsewhere in Warmia and Masuria.
